Structural only: it inspects the shape and the"] # [doc = " values of `d` against `S` and nothing else."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " A negative outcome is a verdict and not an error — the document was"] # [doc = " exactly the kind of thing the judgment takes, and the answer is no"] # [doc = " (´[ROOT-crit:xchg:error-or-verdict]´)."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{satisfies_global, Content, Document, Envelope, NamespaceLabel, Version};"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let label = NamespaceLabel::parse(\"com.example\").expect(\"a label\");"] # [doc = " let document = Document::new(Envelope::new(label, Version::new(1, 0, 0)), Content::new());"] # [doc = " assert!(satisfies_global(&document).holds());"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum Satisfaction { # [doc = " The document satisfies the theory."] Holds , # [doc = " It does not, and here is every way it failed, in ascending key"] # [doc = " order."] Fails (Vec < Mismatch >) , }

# [doc = " One way a document failed a theory, located by content key where the"] # [doc = " failure has one."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Keys 0 and 1 belong to the envelope and are no content keys, so"] # [doc = " [`Mismatch::key`] is `None` for a failure at either; [`Mismatch::at`]"] # [doc = " names the position in every case."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{"] # [doc = "     satisfies, Content, ContentKey, Document, Envelope, NamespaceLabel, Satisfaction, Theory,"] # [doc = "     Value, Version,"] # [doc = " };"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let theory = Theory::parse(r#\"e = {0 => \"com.example\", 1 => [1, 0, uint], 2 => tstr}\"#)"] # [doc = "     .expect(\"an assignable theory\");"] # [doc = " let label = NamespaceLabel::parse(\"com.example\").expect(\"a label\");"] # [doc = " let mut content = Content::new();"] # [doc = " content.insert(ContentKey::new(2).expect(\"a content key\"), Value::Unsigned(7));"] # [doc = " let document = Document::new(Envelope::new(label, Version::new(1, 0, 0)), content);"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let Satisfaction::Fails(mismatches) = satisfies(&document, &theory) else {"] # [doc = "     panic!(\"a uint is no tstr\")"] # [doc = " };"] # [doc = " assert_eq!(mismatches[0].key().map(|key| key.get()), Some(2));"] # [doc = " assert_eq!(mismatches[0].expected(), \"tstr\");"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] # [non_exhaustive] pub struct Mismatch { key : Option < ContentKey > , at : Box < str > , expected : Box < str > , found : Box < str > , kind : MismatchKind , }

# [doc = " One way a later minor fails to extend an earlier one additively."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Every breach carries the content key it concerns, which is what makes it"] # [doc = " a located verdict rather than a bare negative."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{Inclusion, InclusionBreach, Theory, check_inclusion};"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let earlier = Theory::parse(r#\"e = {0 => \"com.example\", 1 => [1, 0, uint], 2 => tstr}\"#)"] # [doc = "     .expect(\"an assignable theory\");"] # [doc = " let later = Theory::parse(r#\"e = {0 => \"com.example\", 1 => [1, 1, uint]}\"#)"] # [doc = "     .expect(\"an assignable theory\");"] # [doc = " match check_inclusion(&earlier, &later).expect(\"comparable\") {"] # [doc = "     Inclusion::Violated(breaches) => assert!(matches!("] # [doc = "         breaches.as_slice(),"] # [doc = "         [InclusionBreach::KeyDropped { key }] if key.get() == 2"] # [doc = "     )),"] # [doc = "     Inclusion::Holds => panic!(\"dropping a content key is a breach\"),"] # [doc = " }"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] # [non_exhaustive] pub enum InclusionBreach { # [doc = " A content key of the earlier theory is absent from the later one."] KeyDropped { # [doc = " The key the later theory does not carry."] key : ContentKey , } , # [doc = " A shared key's type is not identical."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The two strings are the compared forms: the normalized print of the"] # [doc = " type expression, followed by the printed body of every rule it"] # [doc = " reaches. They are diagnostics, not a promised format."] TypeChanged { # [doc = " The key whose type moved."] key : ContentKey , # [doc = " What the earlier theory writes there."] earlier : String , # [doc = " What the later theory writes there."] later : String , } , # [doc = " A shared key's requiredness is not identical."] RequirednessChanged { # [doc = " The key whose requiredness moved."] key : ContentKey , # [doc = " Whether the earlier theory required it."] earlier : bool , # [doc = " Whether the later theory requires it."] later : bool , } , # [doc = " A key new at the later minor is not optional."] NewKeyRequired { # [doc = " The key the later theory added as required."] key : ContentKey , } , }

# [doc = " Where a token or a syntax tree node sits in the source."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Byte offsets slice the source; the line and column locate the *start*"] # [doc = " for a human, both 1-based, the column counted in characters rather than"] # [doc = " bytes so that a multi-byte name does not push the reported column past"] # [doc = " what the reader sees."] # [derive (Copy , Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] pub (crate) struct Span { # [doc = " Byte offset of the first byte."] pub (crate) start : usize , # [doc = " Byte offset one past the last byte."] pub (crate) end : usize , # [doc = " 1-based line of [`Span::start`]."] pub (crate) line : u32 , # [doc = " 1-based character column of [`Span::start`]."] pub (crate) column : u32 , }

# [doc = " A numeric literal, kept as it was written."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The lexeme is carried verbatim rather than converted, because a"] # [doc = " normalized printing that turned `0x18` into `24` or `1.0` into `1`"] # [doc = " would be rewriting the theory rather than laying it out. # [doc = " Filesystem identity of a redirection target."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " This is the **sole** package-local exception to lexical output-role"] # [doc = " comparison `(´guide:execwrap:execwrap´)`, which requires the"] # [doc = " exception to state four things:"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " **The exact hazard.** Two redirection routes resolving to one file"] # [doc = " are opened independently, each with truncation, and then written"] # [doc = " concurrently by the wrapper as the child produces output. The"] # [doc = " result is one log with interleaved and partially overwritten"] # [doc = " bytes, and no I/O call fails at any point. The damage is done to"] # [doc = " the operation's own output, not to repository state."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " **The additional check.** Each target is resolved to a filesystem"] # [doc = " identity before anything is opened: device and inode for an"] # [doc = " existing file (so symlinks and hard links collapse), and resolved"] # [doc = " parent directory plus file name for one that does not exist yet."] # [doc = " A dangling symlink resolves to its ultimate target, because"] # [doc = " creating the file would follow the link."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " **Why lexical uniqueness is insufficient here.** Lexical"] # [doc = " comparison catches `a.log` against `./a.log`, but not two names"] # [doc = " hard-linked to one file, nor two paths beneath a symlinked"] # [doc = " directory, nor a dangling link and the name it points at. Those"] # [doc = " all produce the interleaving above, and unlike an ordinary output"] # [doc = " role — which the caller controls end to end — these paths are"] # [doc = " routinely assembled by build glue where such aliases arise by"] # [doc = " accident."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " **The remaining host race.** None of this closes a"] # [doc = " time-of-check/time-of-use window: the host may replace or remount"] # [doc = " any of these paths between the check and the open. This is a"] # [doc = " preflight guard against configuration mistakes and nothing more."] # [doc = " It is a package-local correctness measure, never a"] # [doc = " repository-wide filesystem security claim."] # [derive (Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] enum FileIdentity { # [doc = " The target exists: device and inode numbers (symlinks"] # [doc = " followed, hard links share the pair)."] Existing (u64 , u64) , # [doc = " The target does not exist yet: resolved parent directory plus"] # [doc = " final file name."] Pending (PathBuf , OsString) , }

class_decisions.name: public-interchange
class_decisions.premises: Public canonical values, theories and registry data are recorded at their consuming boundaries. The Debug structural carrier preserves constructors, sequences, keys and literal contents as tagged JSON; lazy capabilities are described without advancing them. Canonical laws and iterator order remain binding inputs, never observation outputs.

class_decisions.name: public-documents
class_decisions.premises: Dataset input, template sources, projected values and rendered reports are public. The consuming document boundaries preserve available value structure; serde capability adapters inherit those boundaries without adding bounds or invoking deserializers twice.

class_decisions.name: public-execwrap
class_decisions.premises: Child arguments, configuration, outcomes and I/O are public. Tagged UTF-8/base64 preserves original bytes; relays write their original buffers. Read, Write and notification capabilities are not invoked for observation.

class_decisions.name: public-cli
class_decisions.premises: Control records, argv, public errors and serialized output are recorded at command boundaries. Parser and callback capabilities are described without an extra invocation. Non-string panic payloads have no introspection contract and are explicitly unavailable.

class_decisions.name: delivery
class_decisions.premises: The observer owns queue admission, timestamps, metric accounting, encoding, artifact publication and export. These bodies run under the labelled command operation and never recursively instrument observation. Public payload representation changes do not feed a binding return; delivery failures count loss. Artifact publication occurs only on the delivery worker. Full content is a capability selected by PN_OBSERVE_LEVEL=trace. Default span visits retain only command identity and outcome and never call payload Debug; command completion, WARN/ERROR, summaries and status remain emitted. Successful writes and whole-record loss are separately counted.

class_decisions.name: value-traits
class_decisions.premises: Hash, comparison, clone and teardown are structural plumbing inherited by the canonical coding and theory operations that consume the same value. The class inherits the complete set of declared interchange boundaries, including registry acquisition and its CDDL parsing. These bodies preserve their pre-observation implementation and introduce no fresh full-value record. Direct external consumers owe the same labelled caller boundary.

class_decisions.name: secret-carriers
class_decisions.premises: Protected carriers and export credentials expose only role and marker. No production ExposeSecret consumer is admitted. Adding a field, consumer or transport invalidates this body/type-bound admission.

class_decisions.name: public-records
class_decisions.premises: Internal records are public structural carriers. Validation records complete candidate acts and the caller-supplied resolution set, then its typed result; borrowed access records the unchanged complete acts. No codec, subscriber installation, secret acquisition or ExposeSecret consumer occurs. Structural Clone, Debug, Eq and Ord implementations inherit both labelled boundaries, with no duplicate trace on trait plumbing. External callers owe their own labelled boundary.

class_decisions.name: host-transport
class_decisions.premises: The host transport is a secret-terminating boundary, not persistence. Acquisition, sockets, startup, authentication and cancellation borrow secret-owned buffers; only bounded public placeholders and structurally admitted public frames cross into the upstream driver. Fixed diagnostics preserve their bytes; other whole messages stay secret-owned. This source review is bounded to the declared fixture and protocol profile; independent integration admission remains held.

class_decisions.name: host-storage
class_decisions.premises: Storage accepts public validated carriers and returns complete canonical packages and typed fieldless causes. The private Session is not formatted into public content. Closed SQL selects only schema identity and public history; every statement and decoded result is covered by the positive and sensitive DataRow controls. No storage computation reads observation. Async boundaries enter only when polled. Independent production admission remains held.

class_decisions.name: wallet-decoder
class_decisions.premises: Public layout operations and closed genesis RPC reads share the WALLET devnet owner. RPC configuration, connection details and cookie bytes are secret-owned, and the Basic field leaves its carrier only under its caveat; received heads and bodies are public service data held as ordinary bytes; role-only formatting and typed local failures expose no private fields. Under the host-secured path, Elements is a trusted service and parsed chain objects and diagnostics are public. Trace retains complete public input and result; default records outcomes and refusal diagnostics. No signing, verification, spending or recognition authority is admitted.

class_decisions.name: graph-partition
class_decisions.premises: Partition accepts only immutable public BoundaryInputs supplied by records; its Debug includes complete public acts and closures. The return retains structural identities, one least shared identity per intersection edge and complete block vectors. No input or output contains a secret carrier, no graph result feeds observation back into computation, and no serializer or canonical publication path is exposed. Invocation totals and inclusive durations are observed; algorithmic work and allocation bounds are not claimed.

class_decisions.name: graph-registration
class_decisions.premises: Registration operations consume immutable public records, diagnostic graph values and a declared deterministic public verifier. The verifier Debug and inputs contain public evidence only; no secret key or cryptographic implementation is admitted. Trace retains complete arguments and results, including refusals. Typed graph values are compared against reconstruction; serde bytes are diagnostic only and never canonical or binding equality. Observation supplies accounting only and never feeds computation.

class_decisions.name: graph-affinity
class_decisions.premises: Binary and paired formation consume immutable public records, diagnostic graph values and a declared deterministic public verifier. The verifier Debug and inputs contain public evidence only; no secret key or cryptographic implementation is admitted. Trace retains complete arguments and results, including refusals. Typed graph values are compared against reconstruction; serde bytes are diagnostic only and never canonical or binding equality. Observation supplies accounting only and never feeds computation.
